title.narrative: Timeliness of changes to personnel records and the payroll (months) (PI-18ii)

actual.value: Fully achieved. Interfaces developed to connect the HRMIS and Payroll system with the MOF TFMIS have been developed. The systems will be integrated by the end June 2025.

title.narrative: Timeliness of changes to personnel records and the payroll (months) (PI-18ii)

actual.value: Fully achieved. PEFA 2022 maintained the PEFA 2017 score of A for management of payroll changes (now numbered PI-23.2), both using the PEFA 2016 methodology. Accordingly, the end-target PEFA score has been achieved. Interfaces developed to connect the HRMIS and Payroll system with the MOF TFMIS reached production status although additional work is required to formalize the processes to be used for payroll budgeting and commitments.

title.narrative: Improved accountability of public expenditure measured by the quality of annual financial reports (PI-25)

actual.value: PEFA 2022 reports improvement in the score (now at B compared to C in PEFA 2017) for completeness of financing statements (PI-29.1), noting that the annual financial reports cover the majority of assets and liabilities (except the Public Investment Program and financial performance of state-owned enterprises). There is no changes since the last PEFA assessment. New financial reporting forms, complying withe international standards are introduced. Most likely, the score B+ will be achieved.

title.narrative: Improved accountability of public expenditure measured by the quality of annual financial reports (PI-25)

actual.value: PEFA 2022 reports improvement in the score (now at B compared to C in PEFA 2017) for completeness of financing statements (PI-29.1), noting that the annual financial reports cover the majority of assets and liabilities (except the Public Investment Program and financial performance of state-owned enterprises).

title.narrative: Improved accountability of public expenditures measured by the quality of financial audit (PI-26)

actual.value: Audit coverage of 75% of central government entities has been achieved , which complies with PEFA score B. Score B is final target of project.

title.narrative: Improved accountability of public expenditures measured by the quality of financial audit (PI-26)

actual.value: Awaiting 2022 report on audit coverage of central government entities representing at least 75% of total expenditures. PEFA 2022 notes that in terms of submission of reports for external audit (PI-29.2), financial reports are submitted to the Chamber of Accounts within 6 months of the end of the fiscal year. PEFA 2022 reports a score of D+ compared to PEFA 2017 score of C+ (both using 2016 PEFA methodology) for the dimension external audit (now numbered PI-30) primarily due to the observation that the Chamber of Accounts is not fully independent.

Improved effectiveness of PFM IN01315955 â–ºImproved effectiveness of public expenditure measured by the increased alignment of expenditure with policy priorities (PI-12) (Text, Custom) Baseline Actual (Previous) Actual (Current) End Target Value PEFA score D for PI-12 The Law of the Republic of Tajikistan â€œOn Strategic Planning and State Forecastingâ€ is adopted in May 25, 2022, It is expected that the new law will contribute to improvement of aligning of sectors priorities with budget expenditure. title.narrative: Improved control of public expenditure measured by the stock of expenditure payment arrears (PI-4)

actual.value: The stock of budget arrears in 2023 and 2024 was less than 2%, which is PEFA score A. However, data on stock of arrears is not published. It is provided to external audit, the Government and the Parliament of Republic of Tajikistan.

title.narrative: Improved control of public expenditure measured by the stock of expenditure payment arrears (PI-4)

actual.value: With respect to the target level of stock of expenditure arrears for 2023, the PEFA 2022 noted that as of 2020, the stock of expenditure arrears stood at 2.3% in 2020 - near the end-target of no more than 2%. PEFA 2022 reports a score of C+ for stock and monitoring of expenditure payment arrears, no change from PEFA 2017 (both using the PEFA 2016 methodology and now numbered as PI-22 instead of PI-4). Data on stock of arrears is not published, but is provided to external audit, the Government and the Parliament of Republic of Tajikistan.

title.narrative: The number of services available through e-Governance system

baseline.value: No services available on e-Gov system

actual.value: The e-gov portal contains live links to 5 existing electronic public services (e-visa, public procurement, licenses, tax services, and customs import certificates) and 20 static services. The platform has been developed and currently is maintained by new Agency for Innovation and Digitalization.

title.narrative: The number of services available through e-Governance system

baseline.value: No services available on e-Gov system

actual.value: The e-gov portal contains live links to 5 existing electronic public services (e-visa, public procurement, licenses, tax services, and customs import certificates) and 20 static services. The platform has been developed but remains a pilot until the proposed new Agency for Innovation and Digitalization is established.

title.narrative: Total value of contracts that were awarded through an open and competitive process (PI-19ii)

actual.value: Fully achieved. 100% of contracts are awarded through open and competitive process.

title.narrative: Coverage of external audit (in percent of total expenditure) (PI-26i)

actual.value: According to data of the Chamber of Accounts the Republic of Tajikistan as of the end of 2020, the central government entities representing 75% of total expenditures were covered by audits. So the indicator has been achieved.

title.narrative: Coverage of external audit (in percent of total expenditure) (PI-26i)

actual.value: According to preliminary data of the Chamber of Accounts the Republic of Tajikistan as of the end of 2020, the central government entities representing 75% of total expenditures were covered by audits. Awaiting updates for CY21 and CY22. PEFA 2022 maintained the PEFA 2017 score of C for audit coverage a standards (now numbered PI-30.1), both using the PEFA 2016 methodology. PEFA 2022 noted the Chamber of Accounts has audited financial reports of the majority of central government entities, accounting for 64.1% of total government expenditure and revenue during 2018-2020. Audits covered revenue, expenditure, and debt, highlighting relevant significant issues, and were based on national ISSAI-compliant standards.

title.narrative: Additional functionalities (modules) of TFMIS (commitment control, cash management, payment order processing, assets management and payroll management) installed and operational

baseline.value: none of the 5 modules are operational

actual.value: Three modules are operational: cash management (M1), commitment control/liability management (M2), and asset management (M3). Assets management module is not fully operational. Center for Information Technologies of MoF is helping to fully operationalize the module. Payroll module is operational. Also accounting module will be introduced in June 2025. The indicator will be achieved.

title.narrative: Additional functionalities (modules) of TFMIS (commitment control, cash management, payment order processing, assets management and payroll management) installed and operational

baseline.value: none of the 5 modules are operational

actual.value: Three modules are operational: cash management (M1), commitment control/liability management (M2), and asset management (M3). However, they have yet to be rolled-out. In addition, the interfaces developed to connect the HRMIS and TFMIS has reached production stage and require additional work to formalize the processes to be used for budgeting and commitments.

title.narrative: Evidence of follow up on audit recommendations (in percent of audit recommendations) (PI-26iii)

actual.value: Fully achieved. 100% of audit recommendations are followed up.

title.narrative: Evidence of follow up on audit recommendations (in percent of audit recommendations) (PI-26iii)

actual.value: Fully achieved. PEFA 2022 maintained the PEFA 2017 score of B for on external audit follow-up (now numbered PI-30.3), both using the PEFA 2016 methodology. Moreover, as of the end of 2021, the accomplishment of the audit recommendations is evaluated at the level of 100%. Under the Development Strategy of the Chamber of Accounts of the Republic of Tajikistan for 2019-2023, a procedure for monitoring the accomplishment of audit recommendations has been introduced, including the audit reporting form was updated with further involvement of responsible persons participating in the audit process (both audited persons and auditors). The launch of the accomplishment of the audit recommendations is also foreseen in the specialized audit software. Analysis of the updated form for audit reporting, with further involvement of responsible persons participated in the audit process (both audited persons and auditors), shows that that the recommendations on conducted audits are accomplished by all.

title.narrative: PIM methodology is applied in ministries covering economic analysis of investment proposals, project selection, costing and monitoring.

target.value: 3 pilots conducted using the PIM methodology developed by the Project

actual.value: Methodology in place. PEFA 2022 score for public investment management (PI-11) is C+, higher than the 2017 score of D+ from PEFA 2017 (both using the same PEFA 2016 methodology). Based on the study tour to Poland, and in accordance with international standards, Methodological Recommendations (methodology) have been developed ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF A PROJECT REQUEST AND STRENGTHENING MONITORING OF THE PUBLIC INVESTMENT PROGRAM. The software on monitoring PIM will be implemented soon.
